shots.featureName: Build and test a custom prompt in prompt builder
shots.caption: The prompt builder editor
shots.alt: The prompt builder editor with a prompt name, instruction text, and an input added with the slash command, before the prompt is tested.
shots.navHint: Open Power Apps in your environment, then open AI hub > Prompts.
prerequisites: Explore the AI hub and AI model types
setup: Sign in to Power Apps or Power Automate.
Select AI hub > Prompts > Build your own prompt. To start from a template instead, choose a prompt template.
Enter a custom name by selecting the generated name at the top left of the prompt.
Write your prompt with a clear instruction and context, or choose a prompt template.
Include an input by typing / or selecting Add content, then select Text or Image or document in the Input section.
Type a sample value for each input.
Select Test to run the prompt and review the response, and refine the instruction if the output is too long or irrelevant.
When satisfied, select Save.

shots.featureName: Add human review to a prompt in a flow
shots.caption: The approval action configured
shots.alt: The flow designer with Start and wait for an approval of text, showing the Title, the Suggested Text from the prompt output, and the Assigned To address.
shots.navHint: Open Power Automate in your environment, then follow the setup steps in the cloud flow designer.
prerequisites: Use a prompt in Power Automate and Power Apps
setup: Open the cloud flow that has a Run a prompt action.
After the Run a prompt card, select +, enter Approvals in Search, and next to the Approvals heading select See more.
Select Start and wait for an approval of text.
Enter a Title, select Text from the dynamic content list in Suggested Text, and enter an email address in Assigned To.
After the approval card, add a Condition with Outcome from the dynamic content list, is equal to, and the value Approve.
In the True branch, add Post message in a chat or channel. Set Post as to Flow bot, Post in to Chat with flow bot, enter a Recipient, and select the Accepted text in Message.
Select Save, then run the flow.
As the reviewer, select Approvals > Received, open the approval, edit the text if needed, choose a response, and select Confirm.

shots.navHint: Open Power Apps or Power Automate in your environment, then open More > AI hub in the left pane.
prerequisites: Explore the AI hub and AI model types
setup: In Power Apps, select Data > Tables, open or create your table, and import tagged text, for example with Data > Get data > Get data from Excel. Or use the Learn sample data (the healthcare_feedback table).
Select ... More > AI hub, then under Discover an AI capability select AI models.
Select Text, then Category classification - Classify texts into custom categories, then Create custom model.
Choose Select text, select the table and the text column, and choose Select column, then select Next.
Choose Select tags, select the tags column and Select column, confirm the separator, and select Next.
Review the text and tags, select Next, select the training language, and select Next.
Review the summary and select Train.
When training finishes, publish the model from the Last trained version section. To tag Dataverse data, turn on Dataverse in the Model settings pane.
In Power Automate, add the action Classify text into categories with one of your custom models, choose the model, and map My Text to the Text input.

shots.featureName: Manage AI Builder credits and Copilot Credits, and fix capacity errors
shots.caption: Assigning credits to an environment
shots.alt: The Assign to an environment panel on the Add-ons tab showing an environment and the number of AI Builder credits to allocate.
shots.navHint: Start in the Power Platform admin center as an admin, then follow the setup steps.
prerequisites: Use a prompt in Power Automate and Power Apps
setup: Read the Overview of licensing and the capability rate table to estimate monthly consumption per scenario.
In Power Platform admin center, select Licensing > Capacity add-ons > Add-ons tab, then Assign to an environment to allocate credits.
To restrict use, clear Allow users to consume unassigned AI Builder credits in tenant settings.
Check consumption on Licensing > Capacity add-ons > Summary tab (Allocation and Consumption bars).

To download the consumption report, select Resources > Capacity, then on the Summary tab select Download reports in the Add-ons section, select +New, choose AI Builder in Choose a report, select Submit, and download the report when it is ready.

If a flow or app fails with a capacity error, check the environment's allocation and the tenant's unassigned credits, compare them with the consumption report, and allocate more credits or make Copilot Credits available.
Review the End of AI Builder credits calendar and plan Copilot Credits for after the end dates.
